items.message: This change introduces a `gating` parameter to `review_workflows.register()` that separates which lenses a repository *has* from which lenses *gate* a pull request — previously one map answered both questions, so the only way to keep a lens off the required check was to remove it from the adapter, which also made it unreachable from `/review <lens>` comments. The diff adds the feature (in `review.py`), documents it (`docs/extending.md`), records it as `GATE-REVIEW-9` in the design tables, adds a…[truncated]

This change adds a `gating` parameter to `review_workflows.register()`, letting a repository declare which of its bound lenses gate a pull request independently of which lenses exist. The implementation fans out only over the gating subset, so fewer model calls are made when `gating` is narrower than the full declared set. From a performance standpoint, the change moves in the right direction: it gives repositories a way to spend less per pull request. The validation path (unknown lens, empty ga…[truncated]

This change introduces a `gating` parameter to `review_workflows.register()`, allowing a repository to declare which of its bound lenses run on the required check without removing them from the `/review <lens>` chat-ops surface. The core security-relevant properties are: the `gating` set is resolved against the live adapter at run time (after binding, before fan-out), unknown names and empty sets are refused with exit 3 rather than silently degraded, and the parameter is deliberately excluded fr…[truncated]

This change adds `GATE-REVIEW-9`: a `gating=` parameter on `register()` that lets a repository declare which of its bound lenses gate a pull request, distinct from which lenses exist. The implementation is accompanied by five new tests covering the main behavioural properties: selective gating runs only named lenses, non-gating lenses remain reachable from chat-ops, unknown gating names are refused before spend, empty gating is refused rather than silently ignored, and the registered callable's …[truncated]
Test asserts `module is not None` after it is used — the assert is vacuous if load() never returns None for a valid path.
Chat-ops reachability test constructs a fresh container after the run — not the container the run used.
